objective: Formalize the intended steady-state Rhino modeling workflow: ChatGPT Web authors the Rhino Python modeling payload; the local AI primarily executes, targets, validates, captures, saves, and reports. Claude must not invent or rewrite model geometry. Codex may author or modify model geometry only when the structured request explicitly grants that authority.
instructions: Treat the user's clarified role policy as authoritative: ChatGPT Web is the normal geometry/script author. Local Claude is an execution/validation operator, not the modeling author. Local Codex may model locally only when the active structured request explicitly authorizes it.
Do not change Rhino geometry/runtime behavior in this phase. This phase is control-plane/protocol/orientation work only.
Read Phase 17 evidence first. Preserve the proven bridge and MCP behavior.
Introduce a canonical controller-authored payload convention under .bridge/payloads/<task-id>/. The normal Rhino modeling payload is a tracked Python file named rhino.py plus a small manifest.json.

Define manifest fields including at minimum: payload_version, task_id, author_role, authoring_model, payload_type, python_compatibility, execution_method, operation_name, sha256, target_document_required, local_modeling_authorized, and notes.
The default modeling authority must be controller-authored-payload. local_modeling_authorized must default to false when absent.

Claude operator policy: Claude may perform preflight, Git lifecycle, target/document isolation, execute the exact controller-authored payload, inspect results, validate geometry, capture views, save artifacts, and report. Claude must not create substitute geometry, redesign the object, or edit the modeling payload to make it work. If the payload fails, Claude records the failure and returns it to the controller.

Codex operator policy: same default as Claude. Codex may author, repair, or materially alter Rhino modeling code only when the active request contains an explicit local_modeling_authorized=true execution contract or equivalent unambiguous authorization. No implicit authorization from being Codex.

Update AI_ORIENTATION.md, .bridge/orientation/controller.md, .bridge/orientation/operator.md, .bridge/orientation/reviewer.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and .bridge/protocol.json minimally so this role separation is clear and canonical. Do not duplicate the full policy unnecessarily.

Because .bridge/protocol.json currently hardcodes operator=codex, change the conceptual operator identity to a generic local AI/operator representation while preserving compatibility with existing protocol 0.3 request/report validation. Do not bump protocol version in this phase unless strictly required.

Add a controller payload guide at .bridge/payloads/README.md explaining lifecycle: controller writes payload+manifest on main with the request; operator verifies hash and target; operator executes exact payload; operator does not silently patch; results/evidence return through the normal branch/report flow.
Add .bridge/templates/rhino-payload-manifest-v1.json as the canonical manifest template.

Add a standard-library-only helper .bridge/run_rhino_payload.py that deterministically executes a controller-authored payload without requiring the local LLM to copy/rewrite the Python code. It must load manifest.json and rhino.py, validate task_id/path, recompute and require SHA-256 match, require author_role=controller, parse/check Python 3.9 compatibility using the existing tool_support.check_code, require an explicit document_id argument when target_document_required=true, and call the existing bridge.execute() host-side path to rhinocode.

The helper must not create geometry logic itself. It only executes the exact verified payload. It must print the bridge result as JSON and return a nonzero exit code on manifest/hash/compatibility/targeting/execution failure.
Use a deterministic idempotency key derived from task_id + payload SHA unless the manifest explicitly supplies a safe idempotency key.
Add helper CLI options at minimum: --task TASK_ID, --document-id PID:runtime_serial, --timeout seconds, and --dry-run. Dry-run verifies manifest/hash/Python compatibility without executing Rhino.
Do not let run_rhino_payload.py accept arbitrary payload paths outside .bridge/payloads/<task-id>/.

Create a non-mutating sample fixture under .bridge/payloads/_example/ showing a tiny controller-authored payload that only assigns result metadata and performs no Rhino document mutation. The example manifest must have a valid hash.

Validate the helper with the example in --dry-run mode and with negative tests for wrong hash, invalid task ID/path traversal, missing required document target, and Python code rejected by tool_support.check_code.
Do not execute a geometry-changing payload in this phase.

Update the controller orientation so a new ChatGPT Web session understands that for real modeling tasks it should author rhino.py itself and commit that payload alongside the request rather than instructing Claude to invent the model.

Update the operator orientation so a new Claude session understands that its job is execution/validation and that failure of controller code is a reportable blocker, not permission to rewrite modeling logic.
Update reviewer guidance so review checks whether the executed payload hash matches the controller-authored manifest and whether any local modeling occurred without authorization.
Create .bridge/evidence/bridge-phase18-001/controller-payload-workflow.json documenting file map, role policy, execution contract, helper behavior, tests, and backward-compatibility notes.

Run python3 -m py_compile .bridge/run_rhino_payload.py; python3 .bridge/run_rhino_payload.py --task _example --dry-run; all requested negative tests; git diff --check; and verify no Rhino/MCP runtime implementation files changed.
Commit implementation/evidence as the work commit and capture RESULT_COMMIT.

Create .bridge/reports/bridge-phase18-001.json with ack exactly BRIDGE-PHASE18-CONTROLLER-PAYLOADS-20260924-82D4A1-OPERATOR-ACK, exact base_commit, RESULT_COMMIT, and branch operator/bridge-phase18-001.
Run python3 .bridge/bridge_cli.py verify-report bridge-phase18-001 and require REPORT_OK.
Commit the report separately, push operator/bridge-phase18-001, and do not merge it.
constraints: No geometry-changing Rhino execution in this phase.
Claude local modeling is not permitted.
Codex local modeling is permitted only with explicit request authorization.
Controller-authored payloads are the default steady-state modeling workflow.
No dependency installation, force push, or merge.
